name: AI Compliance, Law and Regulation
blurb:
AI law is being written in more places at once than any single reader can follow: fifty state legislatures, Congress, the EU, China, and the county commissions and public utility boards that decide whether a data centre gets built. This hub is the index to all of it as this site tracks it.

The sections below are the six ways in. State laws by jurisdiction, with every bill this site has ingested. Federal legislation, pending and enacted. Global laws, with the EU AI Act and China covered in depth. Governance frameworks, from NIST to the WEF, and the compliance pages written against them. Enacted laws, the bills that became law and what they require. And data centre siting, which is where AI regulation is happening fastest and least visibly.
summary: Every AI law, bill, framework and regulator this site tracks, in one place. Six sections: state laws, federal legislation, global laws, governance frameworks, enacted laws, and the local rules that govern where data centres can be built and powered.

children.desc: Every other framework in this section governs what an AI system may do. This one governs where it may physically exist and what it may draw from the grid, and almost none of it mentions artificial intelligence. Five regimes decide it: state power siting boards, which in many states take exclusive jurisdiction above a megawatt threshold and leave a city able to ask but not require; municipal zoning, which can permit a campus of six million square feet and then prohibit any more, as Fayetteville, Georgia did in March 2026; public utility commissions, which rule on interconnection and on whether data centre load may be recovered from residential customers, as Georgia did when it froze base rates through 2028; environmental permitting, where an air permit may set no carbon limit at all because other pollutants fall below federal thresholds; and infrastructure thresholds, below which no approval is required, which is why an eight-inch gas pipeline serving one customer needs none. The page sets out each regime with the records behind it, the tax abatement terms three municipalities have published, and the four different power figures that siting documents use and directories routinely confuse.
